question: Before performing any uterine evacuation procedure, the position of the uterus (anteverted vs retroverted) must be determined by bimanual examination, and the curettage angle adjusted accordingly to prevent uterine perforation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. A retroverted uterus is present in approximately 15-20% of women. If you introduce the curette anteriorly without checking the position, you risk perforating through the posterior wall. Always determine uterine axis by bimanual examination before any instrumentation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Failure to account for a retroverted uterus (present in ~15-20% of women) and introducing the curette or cannula in an anterior direction is one of the most common causes of uterine perforation during evacuation procedures.
